title: Mumble Brushes His Teeth
blurb: After eating honey, Mumble the bear cub is very tired and wants to go to bed without brushing his teeth. But when he runs his tongue over his teeth, he says “Sticky, sticky!” and picks up the brush for a sparkly smile.

pages.text: It was evening. Mumble the bear cub ate honey. Slurp, slurp, slurp! He licked up the very last drop. “Mmm, honey is so sweet!”
pages.ask: Which sweet treat do you like best?

pages.text: Mumble was very tired. His eyes kept closing. “Haaa-hmm!” he yawned. “Can I skip brushing my teeth tonight?” he asked. Mama Bear smiled: “First, touch your teeth with your tongue.”

anne.say: First, touch your teeth with your tongue.

pages.ask: What do you do when you're very sleepy? Is there still something you have to do?

pages.text: Mumble ran his tongue over his teeth. Sticky, sticky! “Uh-oh, there's honey on my teeth!” He stretched to wake up: “Hmmm-ahh!”

mirmir.say: Uh-oh, there's honey on my teeth!

anne.say: Come on, let's have a look together.

predict.q: What do you think Mumble will do now?
predict.res: It could be either! Let's see.

pages.hint: What is Mumble saying? Touch him!
pages.ask: What did Mumble do to wake himself up? Can you stretch too?

pages.text: They went to the bathroom. Mumble looked in the mirror: “Aaaah!” His teeth were covered in honey drops! How many? Let's count!
pages.ask: What do you see when you open your mouth in the mirror?

pages.text: Mama Bear put a pea-sized dot of toothpaste on the brush. Mumble brushed his teeth and wiped off the honey drops one by one. Swish, swish, round and round! Mama Bear brushed a little too.

anne.say: Now it's my turn, let me brush too!

pages.ask: Who helps you when you brush your teeth?

pages.text: Mumble spat out the foam: “Ptooey!” Then he climbed into bed. He felt proud of himself. “Good night, my sparkly teeth!” He slept snug and sound. Clean teeth, sweet dreams!
pages.ask: What did Mumble do before he went to sleep? Can you tell me in order?

kazanim: HSAB.10 (unverified) · Paying attention to cleanliness and order for a healthy life: links why we need to brush our teeth after sweets and before bed to the events in the story.
MAB.1 · Counting rhythmically and by sight: counts 1–5 objects (the honey drops around Mumble's mouth) by touching them and says the number words to a rhythm.
TADB.3 · Analysing what they hear: tells the events of the story (eating honey → brushing teeth → sleep) in the order they happened.
SDB1.2 Self-Regulation · Notices ways to keep up the bedtime routine even when tired, such as stretching, shaking off sleepiness and getting help from a grown-up.
Value · D18 Cleanliness and D13 Healthy Living: sees that doing what needs doing feels good, even when you don't feel like it.
once: It can also be read during Oral and Dental Health Week (21–27 November, date unverified).
Show the cover and ask: “What might Mumble be eating? What will happen next?”
Remind the children of their toothbrushes: “What colour is your brush?”
Say “sticky, sticky” and pretend your fingertips are stuck together; let the children copy you.
sirasi: When Mumble yawns, yawn too; on the stretching page, stretch together and say “Hmmm-ahh!”
On the prediction page, listen to the child's choice; both options can be right.
On the counting page, say the number together with a rhythm at every touch: one, two, three, four, five.
On the brushing page, draw small circles in the air to show the “round and round” movement.
sonra: Wrap up the story with the picture-ordering game: honey → brush → sleep.
Ask: “Mumble was very tired. What did he do so he could brush his teeth?” (he stretched, shook off his sleepiness, brushed together with his mum).
Ask the children to describe their own bedtime routines: “What do you do before you go to sleep?”
In front of the mirror, all say “Aaaah!” together and give a sparkly smile.

sinif.materyal: 5 big teeth cut from white card, yellow play dough (honey), toy brushes that will not go in mouths, a mirror (Toothbrushes are personal and not shared; do not use real toothbrushes in the activity.)
adim: Stick 5 card teeth on the board; put a small piece of yellow dough “honey” on each one.
The children take turns to clean the “honey” off one tooth with a toy brush, round and round; the group counts together: one, two, three, four, five.
When all five teeth are clean, everyone looks in the mirror, smiles and says “Sparkly!”
In the reflection circle, ask: “When do you brush your teeth at home? Who helps you?” Remind them that toothbrushes are personal and not shared.

evSoru: Why did Mumble want to go straight to bed?
How did Mumble feel when he found honey on his teeth?
Which song would you like to sing while you brush your teeth?

evEtk.ad: Round and Round in the Mirror
evEtk.d: Tonight, brush together in front of the mirror. Put a pea-sized dot of toothpaste on the brush. Let your child brush first, then you finish off. Count to five while going round and round on each tooth; visit every corner of the mouth. If you sing a short song, the brushing lasts long enough. At the end, spit out the foam and smile at the mirror together.

guide.aileNotu: Today we read “Mumble Brushes His Teeth.” After eating honey, Mumble was very tired and wanted to go to bed without brushing; when he ran his tongue over his teeth, he decided to brush by himself, and then his mum finished the brushing. Tonight, while brushing together, you can stretch like Mumble and say “Hmmm-ahh!” or sing a short song. At this age it is recommended that a grown-up finishes the brushing; a pea-sized amount of toothpaste is enough, and a toothbrush is personal.
